$comment: §MT-09-SKIP-LEDGER — THE PER-PACKAGE-COMPILE EXCLUSION LIST. Named, shrink-only,
checked in BOTH directions. Read by tools/ga-gate/check-per-package-compile.ts.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. MT-09 ("26 packages fail isolated compilation") rode through two
consecutive register stamps unverified. When it was finally re-measured it held at 26 —
but the recount surfaced a worse fact underneath it: the 9 skips were a HARD-CODED MAP
IN THE GATE SOURCE, not a measurement. The gate's headline read
packages compiled: 85 · floor 40 · skipped 9
which is a comparator reporting a pass without its denominator. 85 was never the
population. The population is 93 tsconfig-bearing packages, and the exclusion list
contained command-registry, core-app-model, runtime-composer and ai-host — four of the
most load-bearing packages in the tree. The true position was 35 of 93 packages NOT
PROVEN to compile in isolation, not 26.
TWO HOLES, both closed by this file and the gate that reads it:
HOLE 1 — the hard-coded map. An exclusion living in gate source is invisible to every
ledger sweep, carries no owner and no exit condition, and can absorb the next package
that stops compiling with a one-line edit that reads as a fix.
HOLE 2 — the AUTO-SKIP, which was worse. check-per-package-compile.ts used to inspect
the error text of a package that had ALREADY FAILED, and if every line looked like a
global-window.d.ts ambient-declaration miss, it RECLASSIFIED THE FAILURE AS A SKIP at
runtime. That is a measured red being converted to a silent exclusion by the gate
itself, with no ledger row and no human decision anywhere. It was live: the 9th skip in
the 2026-08-15 run was geometry-beam, which is not in the map and never was — it FAILED
and was absorbed. The branch is DELETED. geometry-beam now reads FAIL, which is what it
always was.
RULES:
1. This file may only SHRINK. `skips` is capped by SKIP_CEILING, a constant in the gate
SOURCE. Adding a row here alone exits 3 (RATCHET EXCEEDED). Adding a row requires
editing the ledger AND raising the ceiling in the .ts — two files, one reviewable
act, which is the point. Raising the ceiling is choosing to ship an unproven package.
2. A row that starts COMPILING CLEANLY is also a failure — exit 3 (STALE). Delete the
row in the same commit that fixes it. Paid debt must leave the ledger or this file
rots into a list of things that are secretly fine (gate-debt.json RULE 2).
3. EXCLUDED PACKAGES ARE STILL COMPILED. A skip here suppresses the package's effect on
the EXIT CODE; it does not suppress the measurement. An unmeasured exclusion cannot
be proven stale, and an exclusion that cannot go stale is permanent by construction.
This is the whole difference between this file and the map it replaces.
4. Every row needs reason, owner, exitCondition, class and since. A row missing any of
the five exits 3 — an exclusion nobody owns is an exclusion nobody removes.
5. A row naming a package that does not exist or has no tsconfig.json exits 3 (STALE).
CLASSES:
ambient-globals   the package compiles against window.* properties declared in
apps/editor/src/engine/global-window.d.ts, which is outside every
packages/*/tsconfig scope. Not a type error — a scope error. The
single fix for this whole class is @pryzm/global-types (Phase F,
OI-028); paying it deletes SEVEN of the eight rows below at once.
strictness-skew   the package's own tsconfig is STRICTER than tsconfig.base.json
(exactOptionalPropertyTypes:true), so when tsc traverses into
transitively-imported workspace source authored under the looser base
config, it reports errors in files the package does not own.
HISTORY:
2026-08-15 (S3/MT-09) — ledger minted at 8 rows, extracted verbatim from the SKIP_PACKAGES
map in check-per-package-compile.ts. No row was added and none was excused: this is the
same 8 exclusions, now owned, dated, exit-conditioned, and MEASURED. The 9th runtime skip
(geometry-beam) was deliberately NOT ledgered — it is a failure and now reads as one.

ai-host.reason: Per-package isolation misses global-window.d.ts ambient declarations (visibilityIntentStore, commandContext, bimManager). These are declared in apps/editor/src/engine/global-window.d.ts, outside packages/ai-host/tsconfig scope.
ai-host.exitCondition: global-window.d.ts is promoted to a shared @pryzm/global-types package and ai-host references it; then this row is deleted and SKIP_CEILING drops.

command-registry.reason: Isolation surfaces exactOptionalPropertyTypes errors reached through the ai-host cross-reference — same global-window.d.ts scope miss, one hop out.
command-registry.exitCondition: @pryzm/global-types lands AND exactOptionalPropertyTypes is aligned across command-registry; row deleted, ceiling drops.

constraint-solver.reason: Isolation surfaces ai-host cross-reference errors (window.bimManager from global-window.d.ts absent from scope).

core-app-model.reason: Isolation misses global-window.d.ts; the ai-host cross-reference surfaces window.commandContext, window.curtainPanelStore and siblings.

family-instance.reason: Isolation misses global-window.d.ts; the ai-host cross-reference surfaces window.wallStore, window.bimManager and siblings.

family-loader.reason: Isolation misses global-window.d.ts; the ai-host cross-reference surfaces window.wallStore, window.bimManager and siblings.

headless.reason: packages/headless/tsconfig.json sets exactOptionalPropertyTypes:true, stricter than tsconfig.base.json. tsc traverses runtime-composer -> plugin system -> plugins/annotations/ and reports exactOptionalPropertyTypes errors in plugin source deliberately authored under the looser base config.
headless.exitCondition: Either the plugins/ layer adopts exactOptionalPropertyTypes-safe patterns (conditional spread rather than `field: undefined`), or headless compiles against pre-built .d.ts instead of workspace source.

runtime-composer.reason: Same root cause as headless — exactOptionalPropertyTypes:true traverses into plugins/annotations/ source authored under the looser base config.
runtime-composer.exitCondition: Same as headless; both rows leave together.
